Narrative: The variant is a splice-acceptor (HIGH-impact) in tdp-1, an RNA-binding protein with roles in splicing and neuronal RNA metabolism. Disruption of TDP-1 could misprocess transcripts encoding polarity or fate determinants required for AMso asymmetric division, plausibly causing two glial daughters instead of generating an MCM neuron. The provided literature links TDP-1/TDP-43 function to neuronal biology in C. elegans, supporting functional relevance to neuronal fate decisions [Effect=splice_acceptor_variant&intron_variant; impact_bucket=HIGH; EMS_label=non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 40891506, 32531261].
rationale: HIGH splice-acceptor likely ablates normal tdp-1 splicing, and TDP-1 is an RNA-binding factor with neuronal expression; disrupted RNA processing in AMso could misregulate determinants of asymmetric division and lead to symmetric glial outcomes [Effect=splice_acceptor_variant&intron_variant; impact_bucket=HIGH; EMS_label=non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 40891506, 32531261].

Narrative: This is a HIGH-impact splice-donor variant in ttr-13, a predicted cell-surface protein. Loss of cell-surface signaling or adhesion molecules can alter intercellular cues that orient asymmetric divisions; a splice-disrupting variant could therefore plausibly lead AMso to divide symmetrically and fail to produce MCM neurons [Effect=splice_donor_variant&intron_variant; impact_bucket=HIGH; EMS_label=non-EMS].
rationale: A HIGH-impact splice-donor variant in a predicted cell-surface protein (ttr-13) could abrogate cell-surface signaling or adhesion cues required by AMso to adopt asymmetry; loss of such a molecule could bias the division toward a symmetric glial outcome [Effect=splice_donor_variant&intron_variant; impact_bucket=HIGH; EMS_label=non-EMS].

Narrative: SYS-1 is a core effector in Wnt/beta-catenin-like asymmetry pathways that pattern asymmetric neuroblast divisions. A missense variant in sys-1 could perturb asymmetric signaling in the AMso lineage and directly explain symmetric AMso divisions that produce two glial cells instead of an MCM neuron; this interpretation is supported by multiple studies linking SYS-1/Wnt asymmetry to asymmetric neuroblast fate in C. elegans [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; EMS_label=non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 19389360, 21917811, 29962933].
rationale: SYS-1 is an established component of Wnt/beta-catenin-like asymmetry pathways that govern asymmetric neuroblast divisions in C. elegans; a missense variant in sys-1 could perturb asymmetric fate specification of the AMso lineage, producing two glial daughters instead of one glial and one MCM neuron [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; EMS_label=non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 29962933, 19389360, 21917811].

Narrative: DAF-2/insulin signaling affects neuronal development and organismal timing; a missense mutation could alter signaling in AMso or neighboring cells during male maturation, changing the timing or polarity cues necessary for asymmetric AMso division and MCM specification. The gene has documented neuronal roles that make this a plausible, though indirect, mechanistic candidate [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; EMS_label=non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 31619788].
rationale: DAF-2/insulin receptor signaling influences neuronal development and cell physiology; a missense change could alter signaling in AMso or surrounding cells and thereby affect timing or orientation of the asymmetric division that generates the MCM neurons [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; EMS_label=non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 31619788].

Narrative: CYD-1 is involved in regulation of the cell cycle and positive regulation of asymmetric protein localization; an upstream variant could alter expression and thereby disrupt the machinery that establishes asymmetry at division. Perturbation of CYD-1 levels or timing can plausibly change AMso division symmetry, though this variant is upstream (LOW impact) so the effect is speculative [Effect=upstream_gene_variant; impact_bucket=LOW; EMS_label=non-EMS].
rationale: CYD-1 (cyclin) is implicated in the positive regulation of asymmetric protein localization and cell-cycle processes; an upstream variant could affect expression or timing of cyd-1 and thereby perturb asymmetric division in the AMso lineage to produce symmetric outcomes [Effect=upstream_gene_variant; impact_bucket=LOW; EMS_label=non-EMS].

Narrative: FEM-1 functions in male sex-determination pathways and interacts with ubiquitin-ligase complexes (CUL2); a missense variant could perturb male-specific differentiation programs needed for MCM neuron production from AMso during sexual maturation. Given FEM-1's role in masculinization, an allele that compromises its function could plausibly abrogate male-specific MCM fate [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; EMS_label=non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 15082774].
rationale: FEM-1 functions in male somatic and germ-line sex determination; a missense variant could perturb molecular sex-determination pathways or interactions with ubiquitin ligase complexes (CUL2) that are important for male-specific differentiation of AMso/MCM lineages, potentially leading to loss of male-specific MCM neurons [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; EMS_label=non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 15082774].

Narrative: ALG-1 is a central miRNA pathway factor controlling developmental timing and neuronal gene regulation. A missense variant could perturb microRNA-mediated repression of fate determinants during male maturation, leading to incorrect AMso division outcomes and loss of MCM neurons; the literature links ALG-1 to neuronal developmental processes in C. elegans [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; EMS_label=non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 29117550, 23599497].
rationale: ALG-1 is a core miRNA/RISC factor that controls heterochronic timing and neuronal development; a missense variant could disrupt microRNA regulation of fate determinants during male maturation, shifting AMso division outcomes and preventing MCM specification [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; EMS_label=non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 29117550, 23599497].

Narrative: JMJD-1.2 encodes a histone demethylase that affects axon guidance and signaling pathways; a missense variant could alter chromatin regulation of genes required for AMso polarity and asymmetric division. Epigenetic regulators often have broad developmental impacts, making jmjd-1.2 a plausible contributor to mis-specification of MCM fate if its activity is compromised [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; EMS_label=non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 28126843].
rationale: JMJD-1.2 is a histone demethylase implicated in axon guidance and regulation of signaling pathways; a missense variant could alter chromatin states controlling genes required for the AMso asymmetric division or male-specific differentiation, plausibly resulting in loss of MCM neurons [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; EMS_label=non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 28126843].

Narrative: WDR-48 promotes deubiquitinating enzyme stability and affects synaptic receptor abundance; altering ubiquitin-dependent regulation could change stability/localization of fate determinants in AMso. A missense variant might therefore bias division outcome by destabilizing proteins necessary for asymmetric fate specification [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; EMS_label=non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 24356955, 33622778].
rationale: WDR-48 promotes stability of a deubiquitinating enzyme (USP-46) and influences localization/abundance of synaptic receptors; perturbation could dysregulate ubiquitin-dependent control of cell-fate proteins in AMso, biasing division symmetry and MCM formation [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; EMS_label=non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 24356955, 33622778, 32587090].

Narrative: A missense change in CDH-1 (cadherin) could perturb adhesion-mediated polarity signals or Notch/juxtacrine interactions important for AMso asymmetric division. Because cell–cell adhesion is often crucial for asymmetric fate decisions, cdh-1 is a plausible contributor if the missense allele alters adhesive/signaling properties [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; EMS_label=non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 15924262].
rationale: CDH-1 cadherin mediates cell–cell adhesion; a missense change could alter adhesive interactions or signaling at the AMso niche that are necessary for asymmetric division cues, potentially resulting in symmetric glial daughter production [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; EMS_label=non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 15924262].

Narrative: UNC-52/perlecan shapes the extracellular matrix and influences neuronal dendrite morphogenesis; extracellular cues and ECM composition can influence cell polarity and division orientation. A missense variant could therefore indirectly change AMso local microenvironmental cues required for asymmetric division and MCM generation [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; EMS_label=non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 29678816].
rationale: UNC-52/perlecan shapes the extracellular matrix and has been linked to dendrite morphogenesis; an altered ECM could change spatial cues around AMso or mechanical aspects of division orientation, biasing toward symmetric glial divisions [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; EMS_label=non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 29678816].

Narrative: RSP-2 is an RNA-binding protein predicted to be involved in splicing/regulation of development; missense changes in splicing regulators often produce pleiotropic developmental phenotypes. Disrupted RSP-2 function could mis-splice transcripts needed for AMso asymmetric division and MCM fate, making it a plausible candidate [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; EMS_label=non-EMS].
rationale: RSP-2 is predicted to be an RNA-binding protein involved in splicing/regulation of development; a missense change could alter processing of transcripts required for asymmetric fate decisions in AMso, causing MCM loss [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; EMS_label=non-EMS].

Narrative: GPB-1 (Gbeta) contributes to spindle orientation and other G-protein signaling processes; an upstream variant altering expression could affect the establishment of division orientation in AMso. Because spindle orientation is mechanistically central to asymmetric divisions, perturbation of GPB-1 expression is a credible route to symmetric AMso divisions and MCM loss [Effect=upstream_gene_variant; impact_bucket=LOW; EMS_label=non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 36278516].
rationale: GPB-1 (Gbeta) contributes to establishment of mitotic spindle orientation and neuronal processes; an upstream variant might alter expression and thereby spindle orientation in AMso divisions, a direct mechanistic route to symmetric divisions producing two glia [Effect=upstream_gene_variant; impact_bucket=LOW; EMS_label=non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 36278516].

Narrative: SUR-6 is a PP2A regulatory subunit implicated in exocyst-mediated membrane trafficking and axon guidance. Changes in PP2A regulation can affect polarity and trafficking of fate determinants; the splice-region/synonymous change could alter SUR-6 expression or splicing, plausibly influencing AMso polarity and division outcomes [Effect=splice_region_variant&synonymous_variant; impact_bucket=LOW; EMS_label=non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 24192838, 20392746].
rationale: SUR-6 (PP2A regulatory subunit) participates in pathways that regulate membrane trafficking and axon guidance; alterations in PP2A regulation can impact polarity or trafficking of fate determinants during AMso maturation, plausibly shifting division symmetry [Effect=splice_region_variant&synonymous_variant; impact_bucket=LOW; EMS_label=non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 24192838, 20392746].

Narrative: BRC-1 (BRCA1 ortholog) has been linked to regulation of axon regeneration and neuronal responses; while the variant is upstream, altered expression could affect neuronal remodeling or stress responses during male maturation that secondarily impact AMso-to-MCM fate decisions. This is a more indirect hypothesis but supported by literature connecting BRC-1 to neuronal processes [Effect=upstream_gene_variant; impact_bucket=LOW; EMS_label=non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 33593852].
rationale: BRC-1/BRCA1 has been implicated in axon regeneration and neuronal responses; although the variant is upstream (LOW impact), altered expression may influence neuronal remodeling signals or repair processes required during male maturation that indirectly affect AMso-to-MCM fate decisions [Effect=upstream_gene_variant; impact_bucket=LOW; EMS_label=non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 33593852].

Narrative: GCY-5 is a receptor guanylyl cyclase expressed in ciliated neurons; a missense change could alter sensory/ciliary signaling in the head and thereby modify intercellular cues for glia/neuronal fate decisions. A direct connection to AMso asymmetric division is speculative but biologically plausible given neuronal signaling roles [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; EMS_label=non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 19523832].
rationale: GCY-5 is a receptor-type guanylyl cyclase expressed in neurons/cilia; a missense variant could alter sensory signaling or ciliary signaling in head neurons or glia, disrupting intercellular cues required for AMso asymmetric division and MCM fate [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; EMS_label=non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 19523832].

Narrative: TAG-325 is predicted to be a Rho GTPase-activating protein; small GTPase signaling controls cytoskeletal polarity important for oriented divisions. A missense allele could alter cytoskeletal dynamics in AMso and cause symmetric divisions, though direct functional data are not provided [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; EMS_label=non-EMS].
rationale: TAG-325 is predicted to be a GAP for small GTPases; cytoskeletal regulation by small GTPases is essential for establishing polarity and oriented divisions. A missense variant could perturb those pathways in AMso, favoring symmetric division [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; EMS_label=non-EMS].

Narrative: IMPH-1 (IGF2BP-like) is an mRNA-binding protein implicated in nervous system development; a missense variant could disrupt mRNA localization/stability of fate-determining transcripts in AMso. Disruption of post-transcriptional mRNA control is a plausible mechanism for altered asymmetric division, though direct evidence linking IMPH-1 to AMso fate is lacking [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; EMS_label=non-EMS].
rationale: IMPH-1 (IGF2BP ortholog) is an mRNA-binding protein implicated in nervous system development; a missense change could alter mRNA localization/stability of fate regulators in AMso, disrupting asymmetric outcome and MCM production [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; EMS_label=non-EMS].

Narrative: PTB-1 is a splicing regulator; an upstream variant could alter expression and thereby impact splicing of transcripts needed for polarity or fate determination in AMso. Given the centrality of splicing to gene expression, this is a plausible but lower-confidence contributor to the phenotype [Effect=upstream_gene_variant; impact_bucket=LOW; EMS_label=non-EMS].
rationale: PTB-1 is a polypyrimidine tract-binding protein involved in splicing regulation; an upstream variant could change expression and thereby alter splicing of transcripts that control AMso division asymmetry and MCM fate [Effect=upstream_gene_variant; impact_bucket=LOW; EMS_label=non-EMS].

Narrative: TIR-1/SARM1 has known roles in neuronal degeneration and signaling; an intronic variant could perturb regulation. If TIR-1-dependent signaling is altered during male maturation, it could indirectly affect AMso survival, remodeling or maturation signals required for MCM specification, though a direct causal link is speculative [Effect=intron_variant; impact_bucket=LOW; EMS_label=non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 37083456].
rationale: TIR-1/SARM1 has roles in neuronal degeneration and signaling that can influence neuronal remodeling; although the variant is intronic (LOW), perturbation of tir-1 signaling could affect survival or maturation cues for MCMs or their progenitors, indirectly causing MCM loss [Effect=intron_variant; impact_bucket=LOW; EMS_label=non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 37083456].

Narrative: UGT-22 is a UDP-glycosyltransferase; alterations could change glycosylation of receptors or extracellular proteins that provide polarity/adhesive cues to AMso. A missense variant may therefore have an indirect effect on AMso asymmetric division, but functional links are speculative [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; EMS_label=non-EMS].
rationale: UGT-22 glycosyltransferase might influence surface glycosylation affecting cell–cell interactions or receptor activity at AMso membrane; a missense variant could alter such modifications and thereby asymmetric division cues [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; EMS_label=non-EMS].

Narrative: MRPL-10 is a mitochondrial ribosomal protein; mitochondrial translation defects can impair dividing cell function and polarity. A missense variant could thus indirectly affect AMso division by altering metabolic/mitochondrial status, though this is a lower-probability, indirect mechanism [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; EMS_label=non-EMS].
rationale: MRPL-10 is a mitochondrial ribosomal protein; mitochondrial dysfunction can affect asymmetric divisions through energy or ROS signaling. A missense change might impair mitochondrial translation in AMso and indirectly perturb division outcomes [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; EMS_label=non-EMS].

Narrative: IRLD-66 is a receptor L-domain protein of unknown function; a missense variant could alter extracellular receptor interactions affecting local signaling to AMso, but without functional data this remains speculative. The moderate impact warrants consideration but a low prior probability relative to pathway-linked genes [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; EMS_label=non-EMS].
rationale: IRLD-66 is a receptor L-domain protein; a missense variant could alter extracellular signaling to AMso, modulating polarity or fate cues required for asymmetric division, though functional data are sparse [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; EMS_label=non-EMS].

Narrative: SRH-173 is a predicted membrane protein (chemoreceptor family); a missense variant could change signaling in head sensory/glial circuits and thereby modulate extrinsic cues for AMso asymmetric division. This is an indirect hypothesis with limited supporting annotation [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; EMS_label=non-EMS].
rationale: SRH-173 is a predicted membrane receptor; altered chemosensory/signaling in head cells could change local microenvironmental cues for AMso asymmetric division. The missense variant is moderate impact but the gene is uncharacterized for AMso fate [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; EMS_label=non-EMS].

Narrative: NOS-3 is an RNA-binding protein predominantly associated with germline regulation; while the missense variant is moderate impact, its direct role in AMso asymmetric division is unclear. Potential indirect effects on organismal timing or gene expression make it a low-confidence candidate for MCM loss [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; EMS_label=non-EMS].
rationale: NOS-3 is an RNA-binding factor linked to meiotic regulation; although primarily germline-expressed, altered RNA-binding functions can have broad effects. A missense variant could have indirect developmental timing effects that change AMso maturation and MCM specification [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; EMS_label=non-EMS].

Narrative: PPAT-1 participates in purine biosynthesis; nucleotide shortage during division can perturb cell-cycle dynamics and polarity. A missense variant could therefore indirectly affect AMso asymmetric division, but functional connections to neuronal fate are not established [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; EMS_label=non-EMS].
rationale: PPAT-1 participates in purine biosynthesis; metabolic perturbations can affect dividing cells. A missense variant could compromise nucleotide supply during AMso division, subtly biasing outcome toward symmetric glial fate though direct evidence is limited [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; EMS_label=non-EMS].

Narrative: F55G1.6 is an uncharacterized membrane protein with a missense variant; without functional data linking it to neuronal fate or polarity, effects on AMso asymmetric division are speculative and low probability. It remains possible but unlikely to be causal for MCM loss [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; EMS_label=non-EMS].
rationale: F55G1.6 is predicted membrane protein expressed in virL/virR; a missense variant could affect local cell-surface interactions but there is little functional annotation linking it to AMso fate, giving a low posterior probability [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; EMS_label=non-EMS].

Narrative: BCAT-1 affects branched-chain amino acid metabolism and has been connected to neuronal phenotypes; metabolic disruption can influence dividing cells. A missense variant could have systemic or neuronal metabolic effects that indirectly perturb AMso fate, but direct evidence is limited [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; EMS_label=non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 33024014].
rationale: BCAT-1 (branched-chain amino-acid transaminase) affects metabolism and has been connected to neuronal phenotypes; a missense change could perturb metabolic support for AMso divisions but direct evidence linking to cell-fate asymmetry is weak [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; EMS_label=non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 33024014].

Narrative: ULE-3 is poorly characterized; a moderate missense variant in a uterine-expressed gene is unlikely to directly cause an AMso-specific asymmetric division defect unless pleiotropic expression or unexpected function exists. This is assigned low causal probability in absence of supporting data [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; EMS_label=non-EMS].
rationale: ULE-3 is uncharacterized but uterine-expressed; a missense variant is moderate impact yet without neurological annotation, so direct involvement in AMso asymmetric division is unlikely though pleiotropy cannot be excluded [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; EMS_label=non-EMS].

Narrative: TTN-1 encodes a large structural muscle protein; although cytoskeletal integrity can influence tissue mechanics, a missense variant in muscle-expressed ttn-1 is an unlikely primary cause of AMso asymmetric-division specific loss of MCMs. Considered low-priority without evidence for somatic/neuronal expression affecting AMso [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; EMS_label=non-EMS].
rationale: TTN-1 encodes a large muscle-associated structural protein; although it has roles in cytoskeleton and is expressed in muscle, a missense change is unlikely to be the primary cause of AMso asymmetric-division defects that produce MCM loss unless tissue interactions are implicated, so posterior probability is low [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; EMS_label=non-EMS].
